name: Camera (video capture)
plain: Asks to turn on the camera and receive live video.
meaning: Gives the site a live view of the person's face, room and surroundings. Used for calls and photos, but also for identity capture, biometrics and covert recording if the tab stays open.

access.prompt_ui: Chrome: bubble with Allow while visiting, Allow this time, Don't allow. Firefox: dropdown to choose a camera with Remember this decision. Safari: Allow or Don't Allow, per-site Ask/Deny/Allow. An OS camera indicator (green dot, menu bar icon) shows while active.
access.persistence: Chrome and Edge: persistent per origin once allowed; one-time grants end when the tab closes. Firefox: remembered only if ticked. Safari: per session by default, reasks after the page is left.
access.revocation: Padlock icon, Site settings, OS camera privacy settings; track.stop() ends capture; Permissions API 'change' event.
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes need allow="camera"; the grant is keyed to the top-level origin.
steps: Call getUserMedia({video: true}) from a secure context
Browser checks Permissions Policy then shows prompt
OS camera opens and indicator turns on
Promise resolves with a MediaStream of one video track; or rejects NotAllowedError, NotFoundError, NotReadableError, OverconstrainedError

data.update: continuous at the camera frame rate

limits.headline: Can see and record live video from your camera while the tab is open
limits.user_action: You click Start video, Join call, or Scan, then choose Allow in the browser pop up
can: Show live video from your camera on the page
Send that video to other people on a call or to the site's servers
Take still photos or record clips from the video
List your cameras and switch between them once you allow access
cannot: Turn the camera on the first time without your Allow tap
Keep recording after you close the tab; the browser shows a recording indicator while it runs
Use the camera if it is blocked in your device settings
See photos or videos already saved on your device
limits.differs: Chrome offers Allow this time, Firefox lets you pick a camera in the pop up, and Safari asks per site.

story.what_it_is: Lets a website turn on your camera and see live video of you and your room.

marketing.name: getUserMedia
marketing.pitch: Developer docs describe how a page asks permission, then gets a live camera stream for calls, photos and scanning.

marketing.name: One-time permissions
marketing.pitch: Chrome added Allow this time so people can give camera access for a single visit instead of forever.

story.for_you: A small box pops up asking to use your camera. You pick Allow or Block, and a camera dot or icon shows in the tab while it is on. If you allow it, the site sees you live until you close the tab or turn it off.
story.for_makers: Camera access turns a plain web page into a video call room, a scanner or a photo booth with no app install. It is what makes web video products possible, and it powers identity checks that cut fraud and sign-up cost. The maker also gets sharper support, since they can see the problem when a customer shows it.

use_cases.example: You click a Google Meet link in the browser, allow the camera, and your face appears in the call tile in seconds with nothing to install.
Opening a bank account online, the site asks you to hold up a driver license and then take a selfie so it can match your face.
A browser game reads your hand or face through the webcam so you steer a character by tilting your head or waving your hand, and the video never leaves your computer.
You open a web camera effects page, the site puts virtual glasses and animal ears on your live video, and you snap a photo to share.
A glasses or makeup shop uses your live video to show frames or lipstick on your face so you can try before you buy.
In an online exam, the proctoring page watches you through the camera to check that you are alone and not reading notes.
You record a quick screen and face video message right in the browser to send a teammate instead of writing a long email.
A streaming studio in the browser lets you invite a guest by link, and their webcam shows up in your show.

risks: Covert recording from a forgotten open tab
Face scans used for tracking or identity

technical_bounds: Needs a secure context and (Chrome) a visible tab for ongoing capture
Cannot pick a specific camera silently: labels hidden until permission
No capture of raw sensor data: browser applies processing

abuse: Covert recording from a forgotten tab

history.change: getUserMedia restricted to secure contexts (HTTPS or localhost)
Allow this time one-time permission added
